secrets.name: MULTI_TWITCH_TOKENS
secrets.label: Twitch tokens for Multi (written by Connect Twitch)

help.title: Twitch tokens
help.summary: Normally you never enter this by hand: Multi setup > Connect Twitch stores the sign-in in Windows Credential Manager. A vault copy is only used to seed an empty Multi.
steps: Prefer the Connect Twitch button in Multi setup.
The value is JSON with access_token, refresh_token and client_id from the site's Connect Multi flow.

help.title: Discord bot token
help.summary: The secret that lets Multi's Discord bot log in.
steps: Open the Discord developer portal > your application > Bot > Reset Token / Copy.
Turn on Message Content Intent on the same page.
Paste it here; it is never shown again.
help.example: a long string of letters, numbers and dots (70+ characters)

help.title: YouTube access token
help.summary: A Google OAuth access token for live chat. It expires in about an hour.
steps: Create it with the YouTube live-chat scope for your channel.
Paste a fresh one before you go live; Multi cannot refresh it yet.

help.title: AI provider key
help.summary: Optional. Lets Multi ask an AI to double-check borderline messages. Local rules work without it.
steps: Create an API key with your provider (Anthropic or OpenAI). Ollama needs no key.
Paste it here; set the provider and daily limit in Multi setup > Smart features.

_module.title: PinguinoMulti: one chat for every platform
_module.summary: Multi reads Twitch, Discord, YouTube and (optionally, unofficially) TikTok chat into one feed, highlights messages that need an answer, and tracks what you replied to.
steps: Open Chat (the nav item) to see the combined feed: badges, emotes, search, pins, and a reply box that sends to ONE platform you pick.
Open the Multi setup page to connect platforms: Twitch needs you logged in to innocentpenguin.com as the owner, then 'Connect Twitch'.
Discord needs a bot token and channel IDs. YouTube needs an access token. TikTok is off by default and read-only.
Pick a layout (Combined Chat is the one-window option) so your chat windows are saved.
For OBS: copy the stream-safe address from the setup page into an OBS Browser Source. It shows public chat only.
Run the pre-stream check any time; green means ready, yellow is optional or degraded, red would break the stream.

conn-twitch.title: Twitch connection
conn-twitch.summary: Multi reads and sends Twitch chat with a sign-in you approve once. Twitch is the required platform for the stream.
steps: Green (connected): nothing to do. The detail shows which account Multi is using.
Red 'needs_auth': log in to innocentpenguin.com as the owner, then open Multi setup and press 'Connect Twitch'. Approve the permissions on Twitch.
Red 'token expired' or 'subscription revoked': press 'Connect Twitch' again; it replaces the old sign-in.
Yellow 'reconnecting': Multi retries by itself with growing delays. If it lasts more than a minute, check your internet and restart Multi.
Quick moderation buttons (timeout/ban/delete) appear only after reconnecting with the moderator permissions (needs the site update).

conn-discord.title: Discord connection
conn-discord.summary: Optional. A Discord bot reads and can reply in the channels you list. Replies go to one channel only and never ping people.
steps: Create an application and bot at the Discord developer portal, and turn on 'Message Content Intent' (Bot page).
Invite the bot to your server (OAuth2 > URL Generator > scope 'bot', permissions: View Channels, Send Messages, Read Message History).
In Discord turn on Settings > Advanced > Developer Mode, right-click a channel, Copy Channel ID.
In Multi setup paste the bot token and the channel IDs (comma separated), then Save Discord. Or store the token as MULTI_DISCORD_TOKEN in the key vault.
Yellow 'needs_auth' just means it is not set up; the stream is not affected.

conn-youtube.title: YouTube connection
conn-youtube.summary: Optional. Multi reads the chat of your active YouTube live broadcast with a Google access token.
steps: You need a Google OAuth access token with the YouTube live-chat permission for your channel.
Paste it in Multi setup > YouTube > Save, or store it as MULTI_YOUTUBE_TOKEN in the key vault.
Tokens expire (about an hour) and Multi cannot refresh them yet: paste a fresh one before going live.
'waiting: no active broadcast' means you are not live on YouTube yet; it connects by itself once you are.
YouTube has no reply threads, so replies are plain messages.

conn-tiktok.title: TikTok connection (unofficial, read-only)
conn-tiktok.summary: Optional and OFF by default. TikTok has no official chat API; this uses a third-party package that can break or conflict with TikTok's rules. You can read TikTok chat but not reply.
steps: Only turn this on if you accept that risk.
Install the optional 'TikTokLive' Python package for Multi (status says so if it is missing).
In Multi setup tick 'Read my TikTok LIVE chat', enter your TikTok username, Save TikTok.
Gray 'disabled' is the normal state and does not affect the stream.

store.title: Message database
store.summary: Multi keeps recent chat in a local database so search, cards and recap work after a restart.
steps: Green: readable. 'empty' just means no messages yet.
Red: the database file could not be read. Restart Multi; if it persists, close other programs using the Multi data folder, or move multi.db away (a new one is created, old chat history is lost).

file-settings.title: Settings file
file-settings.summary: Multi's non-secret settings (channel, ranking mode, window options) are stored in settings.json in its data folder.
steps: Green: readable, or using defaults when the file does not exist yet.
Red: the file is unreadable (damaged or locked). Delete settings.json in the Multi data folder; defaults are used and you set things again. No keys are stored there.

file-rules.title: Priority rules file
file-rules.summary: Your edits to the explainable priority rules (weights, keywords, muted viewers) live in rules.json.
steps: Green: readable, or using the built-in defaults.
Red: unreadable. Delete rules.json in the Multi data folder to go back to defaults.

queue.title: Message queue
queue.summary: Incoming chat waits briefly in a queue before it is ranked and shown. It should stay near zero.
steps: Green: queue under 200 and nothing dropped.
Yellow: the queue is long or messages were dropped during a burst. It clears itself; if it stays high, restart Multi.
Mentions and questions are never dropped before ranking.

windows.title: Chat windows
windows.summary: Saved windows decide what opens on which monitor. Without any, Multi still works inside the Suite page.
steps: Green: at least one window is saved.
Yellow 'none saved': open Multi setup and pick a layout, for example 'Combined Chat'.
Positions are remembered; if a monitor is unplugged the window moves to a visible spot and returns when it is back.

ding.title: New-chatter ding
ding.summary: Plays a sound on this PC the first time each person chats in a stream, like the Streamer.bot ding. It never writes anything into chat.
steps: Off by default: open Multi setup > New-chatter ding, tick Twitch and/or YouTube and press Test.
Once per person per stream: the list resets after 6 quiet hours, or press 'New stream' to clear it yourself.
Optional: a separate sound for Twitch's 'first message ever' flag.
A burst (raid) plays at most one ding every 1.5 seconds; extra dings wait in a short queue and the rest are skipped.
Yellow 'sound file is missing': pick an .mp3 or .wav file. Silent on an auxiliary PC: only the master streaming PC plays it.

ai.title: Message ranking and AI
ai.summary: Local rules always rank messages (free, instant, private). Optional AI only double-checks borderline messages and falls back to local on any problem.
steps: Green 'local rules': nothing needed.
Yellow 'no AI key': you turned AI on but no key is stored, so Multi uses local rules. Add the key in Multi setup > Smart features, or as MULTI_AI_KEY in the key vault, or switch back to local.
A daily spend limit stops AI calls when reached (default 0.50 USD).
